routing_rule: REPAIR requires HIGH/MEDIUM AND (violates acceptance | turns gate red | makes a published number or claim dishonest). Everything else -> debt, regardless of severity.

findings.claim: The published dark-mode contrast minimum of 6.71:1 is false — two of the seven categories it explicitly names measure well below it, and one banner element fails AA outright.
findings.evidence: The claim appears in commit 3ee3871 ("Measured minima are 4.62:1 light and 6.71:1 dark across banner, legend, item code, badges, hints, links and the button label on its fill") and verbatim in tasks/TODO.md:48. Recomputing from the token block in src/sec10k/web/static/index.html:16-40, 92-99, 123-129: dark `.s-failed`/`.s-unsupported` banner text (--bad hsl(0 80% 61%) on color-mix(--bad 10%, --bg)) = 4.99:1, dark `.b.st-missing` badge on --panel = 5.13:1, and `#banner .src` at opacity .85 (index.html:94) inside a failed banner = 3.92:1 dark / 3.69:1 light — below the 4.5:1 AA floor. 6.71/4.62 is what --dim on the gridded --bg measures (6.74/4.66 flat), i.e. only the neutral text was measured; --bad was left at the palette's raw fill value in dark (index.html:24) and never checked. The failed banner is exactly the URL-mode state the row's acceptance criterion names ("URL mode still fails loudly").
findings.repro: python3 -c on the hsl() values at src/sec10k/web/static/index.html:16-40 with a WCAG 2.x relative-luminance ratio; compare against the numbers in tasks/TODO.md:48. Confirmed values: dark s-failed 4.99, dark .b.st-missing 5.13, dark #banner .src 3.92, light #banner .src 3.69.
findings.acceptance: Either the published minima are corrected to the real measured floor across all named categories (including --bad and the opacity-.85 `.src` span), or --bad/`.src` are adjusted so the stated 6.71:1 dark / 4.62:1 light claim actually holds; the number that ships in TODO.md and the commit message must be reproducible from the token block.
findings.route_reason: published number dishonest: the 6.71/4.62 minima ship in tasks/TODO.md and commit 3ee3871, and states the audit never visited fall below them; the failed-banner state is also named in the acceptance criteria

findings.claim: The diff size published in the ledger row, `+129/−~60`, is wrong; the real churn is +93/−36.
findings.evidence: tasks/TODO.md:48 reads "`src/sec10k/web/static/index.html` only (+129/−~60)". `git diff main...task/S3 --numstat -- src/sec10k/web/static/index.html` returns `93 36`, and `gh pr view 18 --json files` reports additions 93 / deletions 36. 129 is the additions+deletions total misreported as additions, and 60 matches nothing.
findings.acceptance: tasks/TODO.md:48 states +93/−36 (or drops the count); every number in the ledger row reproduces from a command a reviewer can run.
findings.route_reason: published number dishonest: +129/-~60 reproduces from no command

findings.claim: Two defects the author reports finding and fixing in this diff produced no eval case and no red-watch, violating CLAUDE.md hard rule 2, and the absence of any mechanical check is the direct cause of R1.
findings.evidence: tasks/TODO.md:48 and commit 3ee3871 both state "Two defects found and fixed during the pass, both mine, both introduced by this diff" — (1) the `button:hover` / `.it[aria-current]` specificity collision, (2) light-palette fill colors used as text at 2.40–3.51:1. `git diff main...task/S3 --stat` shows zero files added under evals/adversarial/ or evals/golden/. CLAUDE.md hard rule 2: "Every new failure becomes a case in evals/adversarial/ before it is fixed. Watch the new case fail first." Both defects are mechanically checkable without a browser (a contrast computation over the `:root`/`@media` token block; a selector-scoping assertion that `button:hover` is written `button:not(.it):hover`) — and because neither exists, the contrast number in R1 shipped wrong.
findings.repro: git diff main...task/S3 --stat | grep evals/adversarial  -> no output. Then: the contrast script in R1 reproduces the miss that no case caught.
findings.acceptance: An adversarial case (a small python check over src/sec10k/web/static/index.html, wired into the invariant or fast suite) that goes red against the pre-fix token block for the light fill colors and against an unscoped `button:hover` rule, with the red run recorded before the fix — or an explicit ADR ruling that UI styling is out of the eval set's reach, which then makes R4's browser evidence mandatory.
findings.route_reason: CLAUDE.md hard rule 2 binds, and R1's repair cannot be watched red without exactly the check this finding asks for -- the two are one fix

findings.claim: The row's own acceptance criterion — three input modes re-driven in a browser "with a screenshot" — is not satisfied by anything in the PR; the sole validation for this row is unverifiable prose.
findings.evidence: tasks/TODO.md:48 Validation column: "all three input modes re-driven in a browser against the local app, with a screenshot". The same row's Status column then says "Screenshots were taken in-session, not committed". `git diff main...task/S3 --stat` lists 7 files: 4 evals/report JSONs, index.html, DONE.md, TODO.md — no image, no evidence pack. The row also cites an upload of "a synthetic 4-item filing -> `ambiguous`, 4 extracted / 17 missing / 2 omitted", but that file is not committed either, and per src/sec10k/extract.py:138-143 a 4-extracted document only reaches `ambiguous` if an AMBIGUOUS_CODES validator fired — the claim is neither reproducible nor derivable. (The one claim I could check does hold: aapl-2025 returns doc_status=success, 18 extracted / 5 IBR, 23 items.)
findings.repro: git diff main...task/S3 --stat  (no screenshot or evidence artifact); python3 -c "from src.sec10k.extract import extract_items; from src.sec10k.web import view; print(view.build_view(extract_items('evals/fixtures/aapl-2025/filing.htm'))['counts'])" verifies only the fixture mode.
findings.acceptance: The three screenshots (or an equivalent committed evidence artifact) land in the PR, and the synthetic upload fixture is committed under evals/fixtures/ so the 4/17/2 -> `ambiguous` claim is reproducible — or the acceptance criterion in tasks/TODO.md:48 is rewritten to what the PR actually delivers.
findings.route_reason: violates the task's own acceptance criteria verbatim (screenshot evidence; reproducible three-mode walk)

findings.claim: Dark is now the default theme but the page never declares `color-scheme`, so every UA-rendered control internal still paints in the light scheme on a near-black canvas.
findings.evidence: src/sec10k/web/static/index.html:15-40 makes the near-black palette the `:root` default with light behind `@media (prefers-color-scheme:light)` — the inverse of main, where light was the default. `grep -n color-scheme` on the new file returns only the two media queries; there is no `color-scheme:dark` / `color-scheme:light dark` declaration. Concretely: `input[type=file]` (index.html:79-81, markup line ~110) gets `background:var(--bg)` = hsl(220 34% 4%) while its `::file-selector-button` and "No file chosen" chrome stay UA-light; Safari and pre-121 Chrome ignore the `scrollbar-width`/`scrollbar-color` on index.html:42 (Firefox-only properties) and render light scrollbars over `pre.text` and `details pre`; `<select>` popup, autofill and the UA focus ring likewise. At main this only bit users whose OS was dark; now it is the default path for every visitor including one with no OS preference.
findings.repro: Open http://localhost:8000/ with the OS set to dark (or no preference) and look at the file-input control in the upload mode row; compare with the same page after adding `color-scheme:dark` to `:root`.
findings.acceptance: `:root{color-scheme:dark}` with `@media (prefers-color-scheme:light){:root{color-scheme:light}}` (or `color-scheme:light dark`), so the file-selector button, select popup, scrollbars and autofill follow the authored theme in Safari and Chrome as well as Firefox.
findings.route_reason: this diff flipped the default theme from light to dark, so the light UA controls on a near-black canvas are a regression it introduced, in the upload control the acceptance criteria name

findings.claim: The page now hard-depends on two third-party origins for its typography while the commit and the ledger row both claim it "was one self-contained file and stays one", and nothing verifies the fallback.
findings.evidence: src/sec10k/web/static/index.html:8-10 adds `preconnect` to fonts.googleapis.com and fonts.gstatic.com plus a blocking `<link>` stylesheet; at main the page used only `-apple-system`/`ui-monospace` system stacks and rendered identically with the network off. Commit 3ee3871: "The page was one self-contained file and stays one." No CSP is set (`grep -rn "Content-Security" src/sec10k/web/*.py` -> no match), so nothing breaks today, but on a locked-down or offline reviewer instance the JetBrains Mono stack, the `zero` slashed-zero and the entire typographic premise of the restyle silently fall back to `ui-monospace` (index.html:28, 44-45) — a state no check exercises. The deployed Zeabur instance (tasks/TODO.md S2) would also make an outbound third-party request on every page load.
findings.repro: Serve the app and load it with fonts.googleapis.com blocked (devtools request blocking or /etc/hosts); the page renders in the fallback stack with no indication, and no committed artifact records what that looks like.
findings.acceptance: Either the two font files are self-hosted under src/sec10k/web/static/ (which makes the "self-contained" claim true and offline-safe), or the commit message and tasks/TODO.md:48 stop calling the page self-contained and the fallback rendering is captured as evidence alongside the R4 screenshots.
findings.route_reason: published claim dishonest: "the page was one self-contained file and stays one" is false once two third-party origins are required for the typography

findings.claim: Amber is now simultaneously the brand chrome and the warning/ambiguous status color, so the `.b.lo` "look here" flag no longer stands out from the item code sitting directly above it in every row.
findings.evidence: src/sec10k/web/static/index.html:25 sets `--warn:var(--amber-ink); --amb:var(--amber-ink)`, i.e. both status tokens resolve to the identical brand amber. That same amber is then painted on `legend` (:73-74), `h1::before` (:68), `.it .code` (:120), the `button` fill (:83-84) and the selected row (:117-118). At main, `.it .code` had no color (inherited `--ink`) and amber was reserved for warn/ambiguous. In render() every sidebar row emits `<span class="code">` immediately above `<span class="b lo">`, so the low-confidence flag (:129, `color:var(--warn)`) is now the same hue as the item number one line up. `.s-success_with_warning` (:96) and `.s-ambiguous` (:97) also now differ only by 10% vs 12% background alpha of the identical color.
findings.repro: Extract any fixture with an evidence warning (e.g. a filing where a validator fires) and compare the sidebar row's `.code` and `.b.lo` under the new palette vs. `git stash` / main.
findings.acceptance: `--warn`/`--amb` are distinguishable from the brand amber used for `legend`/`.it .code`/`h1::before` (or `.it .code` returns to `--ink`), so a warning still reads as a warning; and `.s-success_with_warning` vs `.s-ambiguous` differ by more than 2% background alpha.
findings.route_reason: LOW -- scope rule: only HIGH/MEDIUM can trigger repair

findings.claim: The file's own comment says `--accent` is cyan "interactive only", but a non-interactive status badge is painted with it, and one genuinely interactive element is missing from the transition list.
findings.evidence: src/sec10k/web/static/index.html:23 — `--accent:hsl(190 92% 56%);  /* cyan — interactive only */`. index.html:127 — `.b.st-incorporated_by_reference{color:var(--accent);border-color:var(--accent)}` is a static `<span>` badge with no handler, so a non-clickable chip reads as interactive. Conversely index.html:62 lists `button,select,input,.it,a` for the 150ms transition but omits `summary`, which index.html:143 gives a cyan hover (`summary:hover{color:var(--accent)}`) — the skill's hard rule is that every interactive element gets the 150ms transition.
findings.repro: Extract evals/fixtures/textron-2001 (or any filing with IBR items) and hover the `incorporated_by_reference` badge — cyan, not clickable; then hover a `<summary>` — instant color snap, no 150ms ease.
findings.acceptance: Either the IBR status badge moves off `--accent` (or the "interactive only" comment is corrected to name the exception), and `summary` joins the transition selector list on index.html:62.
findings.route_reason: LOW -- scope rule: only HIGH/MEDIUM can trigger repair

findings.claim: `h1::before{content:"> "}` injects generated text into the page's only h1, changing its accessible name for screen readers versus main.
findings.evidence: src/sec10k/web/static/index.html:68 adds `h1::before{content:"> ";color:var(--amber-ink)}`. Chrome/Safari and NVDA/VoiceOver include `::before` text in the accessible name, so the document's sole h1 is announced as "greater-than sec10k inspector" rather than "sec10k inspector". The main version has no generated content on the heading.
findings.repro: Inspect the computed accessible name of `<h1>` in devtools' Accessibility pane on the new file vs. `git show main:src/sec10k/web/static/index.html`.
findings.acceptance: The prompt glyph carries `aria-hidden` semantics — e.g. move it to a separate `<span aria-hidden="true">` sibling, or accept it with the accessible-name change documented; the h1's accessible name should match main.
findings.route_reason: LOW -- scope rule: only HIGH/MEDIUM can trigger repair

findings.claim: The new `:focus-visible` outline is clipped on item rows because the sidebar hides overflow, so keyboard focus in the item list shows only two horizontal segments.
findings.evidence: src/sec10k/web/static/index.html:61 — `:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--accent);outline-offset:2px}` — combined with index.html:110 `#sidebar{...overflow:hidden}` and index.html:111 `.it{display:block;width:100%}`. Because `.it` fills the sidebar's content box, an outline drawn 2px outside it falls outside the clipping box and its left/right edges are cut; for interior rows the top/bottom segments also collide with the adjacent rows' 1px `border-bottom`.
findings.repro: Extract any fixture, then Tab into the item list and step through rows with the keyboard; the cyan ring's vertical edges do not render.
findings.acceptance: Focus on `.it` rows renders a complete, unclipped indicator — e.g. `outline-offset:-2px` for `.it:focus-visible`, or drop `overflow:hidden` in favour of `border-radius` clipping that does not eat the ring.
findings.route_reason: LOW -- scope rule: only HIGH/MEDIUM can trigger repair

findings.claim: The dark-mode hover feedback on item rows is a 1.09:1 background change, effectively invisible, and hovering the already-selected row produces no change at all.
findings.evidence: src/sec10k/web/static/index.html:114 `.it:hover{background:var(--muted)}` with `--muted:hsl(216 26% 11%)` (index.html:17) against `.it`'s own `background:var(--panel)` = hsl(218 30% 7%) (index.html:112) — computed contrast 1.09:1 (main's `color-mix(--accent 8%)` hover measured 1.15:1). Separately, `.it:hover` (0,2,0) and `.it[aria-current=true]` (0,2,0) have equal specificity and aria-current is declared later (index.html:117), so the selected row shows no hover response.
findings.repro: python3 WCAG ratio on hsl(216 26% 11%) vs hsl(218 30% 7%) -> 1.09; then hover an unselected then the selected row in the browser at OS-dark.
findings.acceptance: `.it:hover` produces a perceptible background delta in dark mode (or adds a second cue such as a border/inset line), and hovering the selected row gives some feedback.
findings.route_reason: LOW -- scope rule: only HIGH/MEDIUM can trigger repair
